findings.text: Virtual area flag word distinguishes allocation origin and handling with separate low bits. The ioremap use claims 0x1 [CITED], vmalloc claims 0x2 [CITED], vmap claims 0x4 [CITED], suitability for remap range claims 0x8 [CITED], coherent dma claims 0x10 [CITED], incomplete initialization claims 0x20 [CITED], omission of guard claims 0x40 [CITED], kasan shadow claims 0x80 [CITED], flush plus permission reset on unmap claims 0x100 [CITED], page release on free claims 0x200 [CITED], and huge vmap permission claims 0x400 [CITED].

Deferred kmemleak handling has alternate builds: a build defines bit 0x800 [CITED] requesting delayed tracking object creation, while another defines 0 [CITED] meaning no deferred bit. Sparse areas use 0x1000 [CITED] to mark that not every page is present. Ioremap grouping limit is expressed as offset 7 [CITED] above page shift, noted in source as covering 128 [CITED] pages.

Virtual mapping descriptor known as vm_struct records linkage for early registration or async error freeing through a shared slot holding either a next pointer or a lockless list node. It then carries base address addr, total extent size, flag word flags, page array pages, count nr_pages, physical base phys_addr, caller caller, requested extent requested_size, and on huge-capable builds page order page_order. Linkage uses next or llnode in exclusive fashion.

Address range tracker known as vmap_area holds interval bounds va_start and va_end, ordering links rb_node for tree lookup and list for linear order, a dual-purpose slot that is either subtree_max_size when free or vm when busy, and a flags word marking ram mapping type. Free versus busy membership determines which tree root owns the object and which meaning the dual slot carries.

Cache statistics interface defines a range descriptor with offset off and length len, both wide unsigned, and a statistics record with counters nr_cache and nr_dirty plus nr_writeback and nr_evicted plus nr_recently_evicted. All counters use wide unsigned representation and describe page cache presence and reclaim related states for the queried range.

User mapping ABI defines remap controls MREMAP_MAYMOVE as 1 [CITED] and MREMAP_FIXED as 2 [CITED] and MREMAP_DONTUNMAP as 4 [CITED]. Overcommit policy selects OVERCOMMIT_GUESS 0 [CITED] or OVERCOMMIT_ALWAYS 1 [CITED] or OVERCOMMIT_NEVER 2 [CITED]. Sharing mode uses MAP_SHARED 0x1 [CITED] for shared updates, MAP_PRIVATE 0x2 [CITED] for private copies, MAP_SHARED_VALIDATE 0x3 [CITED] for shared with extension validation, and MAP_DROPPABLE 0x8 [CITED] for reclaimable zeroing under pressure. Header guard _UAPI_LINUX_MMAN_H marks single inclusion without numeric value.

Large page flag encoding derives shift and mask from hugetlb helpers, with shift token aliasing encode shift and mask token aliasing encode mask. Every size variant routed in this lane aliases the matching hugetlb encode token for its size, preserving a uniform mapping from map flag to hugetlb size selector.

Default architecture hooks for huge virtual mapping report conservative behavior. Higher-level huge support queries all report unsupported. Range mapping and unmapping granularity both default to base page size. Supported shift defaults to base page shift. Protection tagging hook returns its input unchanged, providing identity transformation when no architecture override exists.

Public virtual allocation names forward to internal no-profile helpers through allocation hooks. Plain, zeroing, user-accessible, node-bound, zeroing node-bound, constrained address, constrained user, raw, ranged node, plain node, huge node, array, and clearing variants all follow this forwarding pattern, including vmalloc with vzalloc with vmalloc_user with vmalloc_node with vzalloc_node with __vmalloc with vmalloc_huge with vmalloc_array with vcalloc and companions. Huge allocation without explicit node selects the no-node placeholder, centralizing policy in the node-aware huge helper.

Resizing helpers vrealloc with vrealloc_node with vrealloc_node_align and no-profile companions provide node-aware and default-node forms that forward to an aligned core with alignment 1 [CITED]. Public resizing names add allocation hooks around the no-profile core, preserving the same default alignment and default node selection. Node-specific and generic spellings thus share the underlying implementation parameterized by pointer, extent, flags, alignment, and node.

Usable extent helper get_vm_area_size returns total size minus guard page when guard is present, otherwise total size unchanged, keyed on absence of the no-guard bit. Huge-page query is_vm_area_hugepages reports whether the area uses large physical chunks by looking up the area and checking for positive page order, but only on builds with huge vmalloc support; other builds always report false. Commentary in source warns this reflects allocation chunk size rather than guaranteed large mapping entries.

Total virtual space VMALLOC_TOTAL has alternate definitions: addressable builds define it as end minus start, while non-addressable builds define it as 0 [CITED]. Permission-flush marking set_vm_flush_reset_perms looks up the area and sets the flush-reset bit when found, with a no-operation variant on builds lacking virtual space. Per-cpu reservation pcpu_get_vm_areas in the routed stub always reports absence and its release pcpu_free_vm_areas does nothing. Object dump helper vmalloc_dump_obj in the routed stub always reports false.

Balloon accounting serializes on dedicated spinlock balloon_pages_lock held with interrupt state saved across list walks and mutations. Insert balloon_page_insert and finalize balloon_page_finalize helpers require the lock already held and assert ownership. List enqueue and dequeue, single enqueue, single dequeue empty check, isolation removal, putback insertion, and migration fixup all acquire the lock around the critical section and release it after, ensuring balloon list and isolated count and managed counts stay consistent.

Ballooned pages move among free lists, balloon ownership, isolation, and release. Insertion marks the page offline, optionally attaches movable operations with device association, and links it into device pages. Enqueue path also debits managed count and raises inflate accounting and node balloon state. Dequeue path unlinks up to the requested amount, credits managed count, clears migration association while leaving offline sticky, raises deflate accounting, and transfers pages to the caller list. Isolation detaches from device list and bumps isolated count, putback reattaches and drops that count, and migration delegates data movement to the driver callback before inserting the replacement or accounting deflation with zone-aware managed count repair and finalizing the old page.

Exported balloon operations include bulk enqueue returning admitted count, bulk dequeue up to a requested limit returning reclaimed count, single-page enqueue, single-page dequeue returning a page or absence, and page allocation with retry and warning suppression. Movable operations registration accepts only offline and zsmalloc types, rejecting concurrent registration for the same type and rejecting unknown types, otherwise storing the supplied operations and reporting success.

Balloon misuse hazards include silent loss of pages, missing device association, and sticky offline state. Dequeue detects an empty device list with no isolated pages and triggers a fatal bug to avoid infinite driver retry. Isolate reports failure when no device is attached, while putback and migration warn when device association is unexpectedly absent. Finalize deliberately leaves offline set until buddy release. Allocation avoids emergency reserves and retries and warnings, selecting movable high memory when migration is enabled and plain high memory otherwise. Registration uses busy and invalid errors to prevent clobbering or unknown types.

Exported memory-control queries for tracing expose root group retrieval, group lookup from subsystem state, reference release, virtual memory event counters, usage in bytes, memory event counters, page state counters, statistics flushing, and kfunc set registration during initialization. Root retrieval returns absence when tracking is disabled, lookup translates across subsystem hierarchy with read-side protection and reference acquisition, and registration warns on failure while propagating the error code.

Group lookup validates that tracking is enabled and root exists, translates a foreign subsystem pointer to the memory subsystem view of the same group under read protection, and only returns a group after successful reference acquisition. Event and state accessors validate their index against known ranges and return an all-bits-set sentinel on invalid input rather than reading memory. Usage derives from the memory counter scaled by page size. Flush forces pending statistics to become visible.

Initialization hooks wire subsystem operations at boot. Balloon setup registers its movable callbacks for offline page type. Memory-control tracing setup registers its kfunc set for unspecified program type under module ownership and warns if registration fails. Each runs during early initialization and reports status to the caller.

Diagnostic name tables migrate_reason_names with pageflag_names with gfpflag_names with vmaflag_names map internal constants to readable labels, each terminated by an empty entry. Page type labels page_type_names are indexed by high byte minus a fixed base 0xf0 [CITED] after shifting right by 24 [CITED] bits, with out-of-range values reported as unknown. Decoding helper page_type_name isolates the high byte before table lookup, keeping unknown types safe for logging.

Folio helpers centralize mapping and occupancy queries. Mapping lookup folio_mapping returns absence for slab pages and for descriptors carrying flag bits, returns swap space for swap cache, otherwise returns the stored address space. Mapped-page counting folio_nr_pages_mapped returns a negative sentinel when map counting is disabled, otherwise returns the masked atomic value. Diagnostic dumping __dump_folio prints reference and map counts with mapping and index and frame number, plus large folio order and pin state, memory control data when present, type classification among shared kernel same-page, anonymous, or file-backed with mapping details, flag rendering with contiguous-memory annotation, page type decoding, and raw memory dumps, explicitly tolerating races with isolation changes during inspection.

Virtual mapping options carry hazards when misused. Disabling the guard page via VM_NO_GUARD is marked dangerous because overflow loses its trap. Requesting flush plus permission reset via VM_FLUSH_RESET_PERMS forbids release in atomic context due to direct-map work and translation invalidation. Uninitialized marking via VM_UNINITIALIZED indicates incomplete descriptor setup that callers must not treat as ready. Sparse marking via VM_SPARSE warns that presence is partial. Huge permission via VM_ALLOW_HUGE_VMAP only takes effect on builds with huge vmalloc support. Put-pages marking via VM_MAP_PUT_PAGES transfers page array lifetime to free path.
